name: Jecoliah
overview: Jecoliah was a female figure noted in Scripture as the mother of Azariah, a king of Judah. She is identified specifically as Jecoliah of Jerusalem, though her tribal affiliation is not recorded. Her mention is brief, focusing primarily on her role in the royal lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Jecoliah means 'YHWH is able,' reflecting a recognition of God's power. An alternate form of her name, Jechiliah, appears in Scripture with the same meaning. Neither name is indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Jecoliah as the mother of Azariah, linking her to the Davidic royal line through this relationship. No other family relationships are documented beyond this maternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Jecoliah's significance lies in her role as the mother of King Azariah, situating her within the historical and spiritual context of Judah's monarchy. Her mention underscores the providential preservation of the Davidic line through which God's promises to Israel continued. Although not a central figure in narrative events, her identification roots Azariah's kingship in a tangible family lineage tied to Jerusalem.
